subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 34-year-old man has an intensely pruritic eruption of grouped papules and vesicles over his elbows and knees. A skin biopsy shows IgA deposition at the tips of the dermal papillae. He also reports chronic diarrhea and is found to have iron-deficiency anemia.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for this condition?
explanation_correct: This patient has dermatitis herpetiformis, the cutaneous manifestation of celiac disease. Deposits of IgA at the tips of dermal papillae produce intensely pruritic papules, vesicles, and bullae, classically on elbows, knees, and buttocks. Because it is driven by gluten sensitivity, a gluten-free diet is central to management, and dapsone rapidly controls the pruritus and rash. The associated iron-deficiency anemia and diarrhea support underlying celiac disease.

explanation_incorrect.A: Corticosteroids are not the mainstay; dermatitis herpetiformis is treated with dapsone and gluten avoidance rather than steroids alone.
explanation_incorrect.B: Antihistamines may mildly help itch but do not address the underlying IgA-mediated disease or the associated celiac enteropathy.
explanation_incorrect.D: Calcipotriene is a vitamin D analog used in psoriasis, not in this IgA-mediated blistering disorder.
explanation_incorrect.E: Acyclovir treats herpes virus infection; although HSV can trigger erythema multiforme, it is not a treatment for dermatitis herpetiformis.

educationalObjective: Dermatitis herpetiformis features IgA at dermal papillary tips and is treated with dapsone plus a gluten-free diet given its celiac association.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 28-year-old woman with biopsy-proven celiac disease develops an intensely itchy vesicular rash on her buttocks and extensor extremities.
question: Which of the following best describes this disorder?

options.text: Pruritic papules, vesicles, and bullae with IgA deposits at the tips of dermal papillae
Tense subepidermal blisters with linear IgG at the dermal-epidermal junction
Painful target lesions with dusky centers triggered by HSV infection
Flaccid intraepidermal bullae with oral erosions and reticular IgG
Painful erythematous nodules on the anterior shins

explanation_correct: Dermatitis herpetiformis is an IgA-mediated blistering disorder strongly associated with celiac disease. It produces intensely pruritic papules, vesicles, and bullae, characteristically on the elbows, knees, and buttocks. Direct immunofluorescence shows granular IgA deposits at the tips of dermal papillae. Treatment is dapsone and a gluten-free diet.

explanation_incorrect.B: Linear IgG at the dermal-epidermal junction with tense blisters describes bullous pemphigoid, not dermatitis herpetiformis.
explanation_incorrect.C: Painful target lesions with dusky centers describe erythema multiforme, which can follow HSV infection.
explanation_incorrect.D: Flaccid bullae with oral erosions and reticular IgG describe pemphigus vulgaris.
explanation_incorrect.E: Painful nodules on the anterior shins describe erythema nodosum, a panniculitis.

educationalObjective: Dermatitis herpetiformis causes pruritic vesicles on extensor surfaces and buttocks with IgA at dermal papillary tips and is linked to celiac disease.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 24-year-old develops a rash 10 days after an episode of genital herpes. It consists of multiple lesion types, including macules, papules, and vesicles, plus distinctive lesions with concentric rings and a dusky center indicating epithelial disruption.
question: Which of the following best characterizes this condition?

options.text: Stevens-Johnson syndrome triggered by a sulfa drug
Pemphigus vulgaris due to anti-desmoglein antibodies
Dermatitis herpetiformis associated with celiac disease
Erythema multiforme, which can be associated with HSV infection or Mycoplasma pneumoniae
Toxic epidermal necrolysis involving more than 30% of body surface area

explanation_correct: Multiple lesion types together with target lesions showing concentric rings and a dusky center are the hallmark of erythema multiforme. It is associated with infections such as HSV and Mycoplasma pneumoniae and with drugs including sulfa drugs, beta-lactams, and phenytoin. The dusky center reflects epithelial disruption. Unlike SJS/TEN, it does not cause widespread sloughing or high mortality.

explanation_incorrect.A: Stevens-Johnson syndrome involves fever, widespread bullae and necrosis with skin sloughing and mucosal erosions, not isolated target lesions.
explanation_incorrect.B: Pemphigus vulgaris causes flaccid bullae and oral erosions with reticular IgG, not target lesions with dusky centers.
explanation_incorrect.C: Dermatitis herpetiformis is intensely pruritic with IgA at dermal papillary tips and extensor/buttock distribution, not target lesions.
explanation_incorrect.E: Toxic epidermal necrolysis is a severe drug reaction with more than 30% BSA involvement and widespread sloughing, not this self-limited targetoid rash.

educationalObjective: Erythema multiforme presents with multiple lesion types and target lesions with dusky centers, often after HSV or Mycoplasma infection.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: A 32-year-old develops high fever and widespread painful bullae with necrosis and sloughing of the skin at the dermal-epidermal junction. The Nikolsky sign is positive, and there are erosions of the oral and ocular mucosa. The involved surface area is approximately 20%. He recently started a sulfa antibiotic.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnosis?

options.text: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (less than 10% body surface area)
Toxic epidermal necrolysis (more than 30% body surface area)

explanation_correct: Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis are severe, often drug-triggered reactions characterized by fever, bullae, necrosis, and sloughing at the dermal-epidermal junction with a positive Nikolsky sign and mucosal involvement; mortality is high. The extent of involvement defines the subtype: SJS is less than 10% BSA, SJS-TEN overlap is 10-30%, and TEN is more than 30%. This patient's 20% involvement with mucosal erosions and targetoid lesions fits SJS-TEN overlap.

explanation_incorrect.A: Erythema multiforme minor has target lesions and minimal mucosal involvement without widespread sloughing or high mortality.
explanation_incorrect.C: SJS is defined as less than 10% BSA involvement; 20% involvement is beyond that threshold.
explanation_incorrect.D: TEN requires more than 30% BSA involvement, which exceeds this patient's 20%.
explanation_incorrect.E: Bullous pemphigoid is a chronic, less severe autoimmune blistering disease with tense blisters and mucosal sparing, not an acute sloughing emergency.

educationalObjective: SJS/TEN is a high-mortality drug reaction with mucosal involvement and a positive Nikolsky sign; 10-30% BSA involvement is SJS-TEN overlap.

subject: Musculoskeletal
vignette: An infant develops blisters and erosions on the skin after minor friction from clothing, along with oral blisters that interfere with bottle feeding. Similar blistering occurred in a parent. Genetic testing reveals a mutation in a keratin gene.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Epidermolysis bullosa comprises inherited skin disorders characterized by bullae, erosions, and ulcers triggered by minor trauma. Blisters appear early in life, and oral blisters during bottle feeding are a classic clue. It is most commonly caused by mutations in keratin genes. The family history and early onset distinguish it from the acquired autoimmune blistering diseases.

explanation_incorrect.A: Bullous pemphigoid is an acquired autoimmune disease of older adults with tense blisters, not an inherited keratin gene disorder of infancy.
explanation_incorrect.B: Pemphigus vulgaris is an acquired autoimmune disease with flaccid blisters and oral erosions due to anti-desmoglein IgG, not a keratin gene mutation.
explanation_incorrect.C: Dermatitis herpetiformis is an IgA-mediated disease linked to celiac disease, not an inherited keratinopathy.
explanation_incorrect.D: Stevens-Johnson syndrome is an acute drug reaction with fever and widespread sloughing, not a chronic inherited blistering condition.

educationalObjective: Epidermolysis bullosa is an inherited, keratin-gene-associated blistering disorder presenting in infancy with trauma-induced blisters and oral blisters during feeding.
